No option can be put forward yet, because the model could not test your requirement to keep monthly churn **under 4%**.

- The price comparison itself held up under the changes tested, but that is not a check of the churn limit or of reaching £20k MRR within 12 months.
- The model also assumed that higher MRR is the objective, rather than having that direction explicitly stated.
- Its most influential inputs include Pro subscriber count, other-plan MRR, conversions and churn; the underlying values were supplied by Olumi, not measured user evidence.

The central reasoning gap is to connect the churn limit to a measurable model outcome.
